title: Venison with Noodles and Vegetables in Tomato Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines tender venison, noodles, carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy vegetables, all tossed in a flavorful tomato‑based sauce. Venison is a lean source of protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Venison contains less fat than beef and is rich in iron and zinc.
Tomatoes in the sauce provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Broccoli is one of the most nutrient‑dense vegetables, high in vitamin C and K.
Al dente noodles retain their shape and absorb the sauce quickly.
Dark‑green leafy greens such as spinach or kale are high in folate and B‑vitamins.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Venison supplies complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many other meats, venison has lower saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables contribute vitamins A, C, K, folate, potassium and magnesium for overall wellbeing.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and phytochemicals from broccoli help combat free radicals.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Carrots, broccoli and leafy greens boost fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Allergy to game meat
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to venison.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Venison is relatively high in purines, which can be an issue for people with gout.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; those with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Cooking sensitivity
items.content: Venison can become dry if overcooked, so careful timing is required.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing the noodles with the sauce, then adding sliced venison and vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs or grated Parmesan if desired. Ideal as a main course for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Store unused ingredients separately: raw venison in the freezer, noodles and vegetables in the fridge.
